title: Housing tenure changes the monthly resource-and-job transition surface under work limitation
source_unit: Identified 2025 SIPP person, adjacent reference-month pair, conditioned on first-month tenure and work-limiting status

observations.period: 2024 reference year; month t resource band to month t+1 job-count change; work-limited

denominator.unit: selected valid owner/buyer and renter adjacent person-month pairs below 1x poverty

owned_or_being_bought.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.255 percentage points; n=3,920

rented.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.218 percentage points; n=5,704

observations.method: Same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag using THINCPOV and RMNUMJOBS, conditioned on EDISABL=1 and first-month ETENURE; valid ATENURE required; WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR.
observations.uncertainty: Tenure cells differ in composition and the contrast is not standardized; reported work limitation is not a diagnosis or causal exposure.
observations.subgroup: Persons below 1x poverty reporting a work-limiting condition
observations.counterinterpretation: A small owner/renter difference can reflect health, job access, household composition, reporting, or tenure selection rather than housing tenure itself.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; month t resource band to month t+1 job-count change; work-limited

denominator.unit: selected valid owner/buyer and renter adjacent person-month pairs at 4x poverty or more

owned_or_being_bought.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.180 percentage points; n=13,350

rented.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.312 percentage points; n=2,542

observations.method: Same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag using THINCPOV and RMNUMJOBS, conditioned on EDISABL=1 and first-month ETENURE; valid ATENURE required; WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR.
observations.uncertainty: The high-resource renter cell is much smaller than the owner cell; this is not a standardized or causal contrast.
observations.subgroup: Persons at 4x poverty or more reporting a work-limiting condition
observations.counterinterpretation: Near-equal point estimates do not imply equal room, job quality, hours, pay, or schedule control.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; month t job-count category to month t+1 resource-band change; one job; work-limited

denominator.unit: selected valid owner/buyer and renter adjacent person-month pairs with one job

owned_or_being_bought.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.409 percentage points; n=7,194

rented.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.575 percentage points; n=3,485

observations.method: Reverse same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag from RMNUMJOBS to THINCPOV, conditioned on EDISABL=1 and first-month ETENURE; valid ATENURE required; WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison is descriptive and composition-sensitive; resource-band change has no welfare direction by itself.
observations.subgroup: Work-limited persons with one job in the first month
observations.counterinterpretation: Greater resource-band movement among renters may reflect income, hours, transfers, prices, household change, or tenure selection.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; month t job-count category to month t+1 resource-band change; two jobs; work-limited

denominator.unit: selected valid owner/buyer and renter adjacent person-month pairs with two jobs

owned_or_being_bought.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.931 percentage points; n=495

rented.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 1.940 percentage points; n=327

observations.method: Reverse same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag from RMNUMJOBS to THINCPOV, conditioned on EDISABL=1 and first-month ETENURE; valid ATENURE required; WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR.
observations.uncertainty: Both tenure cells are small and imprecise; the contrast should not be generalized.
observations.subgroup: Work-limited persons with two jobs in the first month
observations.counterinterpretation: The point difference may be sampling variation or composition, and does not identify voluntary mobility or insecurity.

related_sources.claim: The unconditioned work-limitation cross-lag establishes the broader transition surface before tenure conditioning.

boundary: Same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag conditioned on official tenure category and reported work-limiting status; it does not establish a tenure effect, household prevalence, disability diagnosis, accommodation, job quality, pay, care, trust, political action, or recovery.
